failure_modes: Selective enrichment of a minor, more robust particle subpopulation by acoustic focusing (apparent preservation of surface markers and particle peaks while bulk protected cargo or functional EVs are lost).

Spike‑in tracer and/or immuno-capture reagents interact differently with acoustic device materials or elution buffers than endogenous EVs, producing misleading recovery/performance readouts (assay compatibility artifact).

Acoustic concentrator elution buffers or device-derived contaminants (leachables) alter downstream capture assays or protease/RNase protection readouts, confounding interpretation of membrane protection.
Acoustic focusing yields insufficient recovered particle/mass at pilot throughput despite preserved signature in small fractions, making it non‑manufacturable even if analytically ‘successful’.
Inter‑lot variability: preservation observed in one or two lots fails to reproduce across >=3 independent conditioned‑medium lots, indicating conditional or non‑robust effect.

Downstream fractionation or formulation incompatibilities (independent of concentration shear) are misattributed to concentration principle, leading to incorrect rejection/acceptance of acoustic focus intervention.

Spike‑in tracer is not representative of clinically relevant EV subtypes or cargo (size, density, membrane composition), so validated spike recovery does not validate preservation of therapeutic payload or potency.
False negatives/positives in protease + detergent protection assays (e.g., incomplete protease access, detergent incompatibility) mask true membrane disruption or protection status.
strongest_objection: The most bounded and plausible failure mode is that the acoustic-focusing arm will produce an apparent preservation of orthogonal intact‑EV signatures by selectively enriching a minor, more robust particle subpopulation or by producing assay artifacts (buffer/device interactions) rather than by preserving the original EV population’s membrane integrity. Because spike‑in tracers, capture reagents, and elution buffers can differ in physical/chemical behavior from endogenous EVs, validated spike‑in recovery and capture-compatibility controls may falsely reassure even while the bulk product composition and protected cargo (the biologically relevant material) are altered or depleted. This would mislead downstream comparability and potency linkage decisions and be hard to detect without multi‑omic protected‑cargo checks, orthogonal source‑matched controls, and multi‑lot reproducibility.
